items.title: Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature
items.summary: Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature on the Apple TV app offering sign language interpretation for supported titles.
items.body:
Sign Language, the new accessibility feature on the Apple TV app, debuts with the global streaming premiere of the film Being Heumann on November 13.

Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app that gives viewers the option to watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation.1 The feature will be available on Friday, November 13, alongside the global streaming premiere of Being Heumann, a film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, on Apple TV.

In addition to Being Heumann, interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will be available for the movie F1. Later this year, Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow, with more Apple Original titles to come. When turned on in Apple TV app settings, the Sign Language option will appear on supported Apple Original titles.

“At Apple, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy great stories and entertainment,” said Sarah Herrlinger, Apple’s senior director of Global Accessibility Policy and Initiatives. “Bringing sign language interpretation to Apple TV is an exciting step forward in making the viewing experience more accessible and inclusive for Deaf audiences. Accessibility is a core value at Apple, and we’re proud to continue creating experiences that allow more people to enjoy the content they love.”

Being Heumann, directed by Academy Award-winning filmmaker Siân Heder and starring Ruth Madeley, chronicles the story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann.

Apple TV offers a sign language experience that’s designed and tested by Deaf and native signers. Each performance is carefully crafted to fit and complement the Apple Original film it interprets.

“It’s incredibly meaningful to see our beautiful language authentically represented onscreen,” said Daniel Durant, who appears in Being Heumann and directed the film’s sign language interpretation. “Bringing this experience to life required a lot of care to ensure every translation captured the emotion and meaning of the story. I’m proud to have been part of Being Heumann and thrilled to see Apple TV supporting greater accessibility for Deaf audiences.”

Titles with sign language interpretation will be labeled with a Sign Language icon, making it easy to know when the option is available. Viewers can enable the feature in Apple TV app settings, then press the Sign Language button while watching. Search will also make it easier to find titles that feature sign language with simple phrases like “with ASL.”

The Sign Language feature on the Apple TV app is easy to set up and offers an experience designed and tested by Deaf and native signers.

As sign language interpretation becomes more widely available across streaming services, the new “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” collection on the Apple TV app will offer viewers a simple way to explore titles featuring sign language, in one dedicated destination.

In Being Heumann, Judy Heumann (Ruth Madeley) — scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden — turns her outrage into a revolution. In San Francisco in 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protesters organize a sit-in to send a very loud message: The system is broken — not us. The film marks the second collaboration between Apple Original Films and writer-director Siân Heder, who directed the multi-Academy Award-winning film CODA, which made history as the first film with a predominantly Deaf cast to receive the Best Picture honor.

Being Heumann premieres globally on Apple TV on Friday, November 13. Viewers can add Being Heumann to their watchlist on Apple TV.

Apple TV offers premium, compelling drama and comedy series, feature films, groundbreaking documentaries, and kids and family entertainment, and is available to watch across all of a user’s favorite screens. After its launch on November 1, 2019, Apple TV became the first all-original streaming service to launch around the world, and has premiered more original hits and received more award recognitions faster than any other streaming service in its debut. To date, Apple Original films, documentaries, and series have been honored with 919 wins and 3,829 award nominations and counting, including Academy Award Best Picture winner CODA and Academy Award winner F1, the highest-grossing sports feature of all time.

Apple TV is available on the Apple TV app in 170 countries and regions, on over 1 billion screens, including iPhone; iPad; Apple TV 4K; Apple Vision Pro; Mac; popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL, and others; Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices; Chromecast with Google TV; PlayStation and Xbox gaming consoles; and at tv.apple.com, for $14.99 per month with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. For a limited time, customers who purchase and activate a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K, or Mac can enjoy three months of Apple TV for free.2

For more information, visit apple.com/tvpr and see the full list of supported devices.

items.title: Football Manager and other hit franchises headline Apple Arcade’s holiday lineup
items.summary: Today Apple Arcade welcomes Football Manager 27 Touch, plus four new games for every kind of player on December 3.
items.body:
Developed by Sports Interactive, Football Manager 27 Touch immerses fans and newcomers in an authentic soccer management experience featuring the world’s biggest leagues.

Available on Apple Arcade starting today, Football Manager 27 Touch puts the manager’s seat in players’ pockets. An elevated Match Engine offers ways to shape the action on the pitch, new Recruitment and Match Preparation tools make scouting and game plans easier to master, and a redesigned iPhone interface keeps everything within thumb’s reach. Football Manager 27 Touch joins a deep bench of standout sports games on Arcade, including NBA 2K27 Arcade Edition, Madden NFL 27 Arcade Edition, NFL Retro Bowl ’27, PGA TOUR Pro Golf, and Retro Bowl College+.

On December 3, Apple Arcade welcomes four new games for every kind of player, delivering a rich mix of reimagined classics, thrilling adventures, and family-friendly hits. Players can fend off waves of the undead in Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted; try their hand at a roguelike twist on a card classic in solitaire(ish); vanquish foes, master time, and explore a mythological setting in Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+; and spark early creative curiosity in LEGO® DUPLO® Playtime. Every game on Arcade is free of ads and in-app purchases, and one subscription covers a family of up to six, so everyone can play this holiday season without interruptions.

Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted brings back the iconic characters, humor, and strategic gameplay that made the original a classic. The game adds new levels, fresh modes, and ways for players to team up with a friend in local co-op and PvP on the same device. The Arcade-exclusive Party mode also gives the backyard a delightful makeover.

Defend the lawn again — or for the first time — in the blockbuster tower defense game Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted, developed by PopCap Studios.

Playstack, the publisher of the award-winning indie sensation Balatro, brings a new twist on a classic card game. In solitaire(ish), players build soaring card stacks to hit rising score goals, collect rare perk cards, and upgrade their decks from more than 150 special cards. With daily streaks, leaderboards, and collectible cards to be discovered, every run feels fresh in a rule-bending spin on solitaire.

Developed by Playstack, solitaire(ish) combines the classic card game with strategic roguelike deck-building.

In the action game Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+, players harness potent time powers, acrobatic agility, and precision swordplay to explore and conquer the interconnected, time-warped depths of Mount Qaf. Available on Arcade with all downloadable content included, this definitive edition delivers the complete experience of the critically acclaimed original alongside new challenges, quests, and cosmetic updates.

Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown+, developed by Ubisoft, comes with all DLC, including the Mask of Darkness story expansion.

Rounding out the December lineup is LEGO DUPLO Playtime, a calm, open-ended digital toy chest where little builders can mix and match iconic LEGO DUPLO bricks to craft a unique living playground.

In LEGO DUPLO Playtime, from acclaimed early learning developer StoryToys, little builders can create custom characters and playful worlds using familiar LEGO DUPLO bricks.

Pricing and Availability

• Apple Arcade is available for $6.99 (U.S.) per month with a one-month free trial. Customers who purchase a new iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple TV receive three months of Apple Arcade for free.1

• Apple Arcade is part of Apple One’s Individual ($21.95 U.S.), Family ($27.95 U.S.), and Premier ($39.95 U.S.) plans, with a one-month free trial.2

• Arcade Originals are playable across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro. App Store Greats are available on iPhone, iPad, and Apple Vision Pro.

• An Apple Arcade subscription gives a family of up to six unlimited access to all the games in its catalog.

• Availability for the 200+ games across devices varies based on hardware and software compatibility. Some content may not be available in all areas.

items.summary: AMD RX 9070 XT 用户称自己观察到的写入速率为每秒 5MB 左右，并且这个过程是持续的；AMD RX 7900 XTX 用户报告的写入速率为每秒 0.7MB。不过这可能与显卡型号无关，主要还是显卡驱动程序造成的问题。 持续写入的数据量取决于写入速率和电脑运行时间，以每秒 5MB 的写入速率计算：24 小时写入请求约为 432GB，连续运行 30 天约为 13TB。当然 PC 不可能 24 小时开机且始终都是空闲状态，所以正常情况下不至于写入 13TB 数据。

items.title: Olivia Dean is Apple Music’s Artist of the Year for 2026
items.summary: Apple Music named Olivia Dean its 2026 Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom over the past year.
items.body:
Apple Music named Olivia Dean its 2026 Artist of the Year, celebrating the British singer-songwriter’s meteoric rise following the release of The Art of Loving.

Olivia Dean was announced today as Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom in what’s been the defining feel-good music story of 2026. She is the first UK artist to receive this honor.

Olivia’s late 2025 album, The Art of Loving, truly broke through this year. Her hit “Man I Need” has charted on Apple Music’s Daily Top 100 every day since first appearing on August 29, 2025. In addition to selling out her global tour, she won a GRAMMY for Best New Artist and four BRIT Awards, including Artist of the Year. In fall 2025, Olivia opened for Sabrina Carpenter at Madison Square Garden, in New York City. Less than a year later, she returned for her own four-night residency and followed up with a six-night sold-out run at The O2 Arena, in London.

Olivia has found and grown her audience with warm, vulnerable songs about love and friendship. Apple Music editors have highlighted the grace with which her music taps into the rich songwriting tradition of 1960s soul and pop, and is inspired by the sensuality of Sade, the brazenness of Prince, and the honesty of Lauryn Hill — all while fostering a community built on love. Olivia’s messages of affirmation and connection resonate deeply with her fans. Listeners have responded to her worldview that expressing love, in all its forms, is an active practice that takes conscious effort, an idea inspired by the 1999 book All About Love: New Visions, by bell hooks.

“I love making music,” said Olivia. “It’s the best thing in the world. I think being Apple’s Artist of the Year feels really amazing. To be recognized as an artist that’s made an impact is really cool.”

“What sets Olivia apart is that she speaks from the heart, every time,” said Rachel Newman, Apple Music’s co-head. “Her songs make you want to call a friend, dance in your kitchen, and tell someone you love them. She is open and genuine in everything she shares, and that connection is what turned a great year into a defining one.”

As Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, Olivia will receive a physical award that represents the extraordinary artistry integral to creating music. Each Apple Music Award features Apple’s custom silicon wafer suspended between a polished sheet of glass, and a machined and anodized aluminum body. In a symbolic gesture, the same chip powering the devices that put over 100 million songs at listeners’ fingertips also sits at the very heart of the Apple Music Awards.

Celebrate Olivia’s Artist of the Year appointment with a special selection of playlists dedicated to the songs and voices that have shaped the last 12 months.

Apple loves music. Apple revolutionized the music experience with iPod and iTunes. Today, the award-winning Apple Music celebrates musicians, songwriters, producers, and fans with a catalog of over 100 million songs, expertly curated playlists, and the best artist interviews, conversations, and global premieres with Apple Music Radio. With original content from the most respected and beloved people in music, autoplay, time-synced lyrics, lossless audio, and immersive sound powered by Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos, Apple Music offers the world’s best listening experience, helping listeners discover new music and enjoy their favorites while empowering the global artist community. Apple Music is available in over 167 countries and regions on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, HomePod, CarPlay, Apple Vision Pro, and online at music.apple.com, plus popular smart speakers, smart TVs, and Android and Windows devices. Apple Music is ad-free and never shares consumer data with third parties. More information is available at apple.com/apple-music.

Olivia Dean was announced today as Apple Music’s Artist of the Year, recognizing her undeniable leap to stardom in what’s been the defining feel-good music story of 2026. She is the first UK artist to receive this honor.

Olivia’s late 2025 album, The Art of Loving, truly broke through this year. Her hit “Man I Need” has charted on Apple Music’s Daily Top 100 every day since first appearing on August 29, 2025. In addition to selling out her global tour, she won a GRAMMY for Best New Artist and four BRIT Awards, including Artist of the Year. In fall 2025, Olivia opened for Sabrina Carpenter at Madison Square Garden, in New York City. Less than a year later, she returned for her own four-night residency and followed up with a six-night sold-out run at The O2 Arena, in London.

Olivia has found and grown her audience with warm, vulnerable songs about love and friendship. Olivia’s messages of affirmation and connection resonate deeply with her fans. Listeners have responded to her worldview that expressing love, in all its forms, is an active practice that takes conscious effort, an idea inspired by the 1999 book All About Love: New Visions, by bell hooks.

“I love making music,” said Olivia. “It’s the best thing in the world. I think being Apple’s Artist of the Year feels really amazing. To be recognized as an artist that’s made an impact is really cool.”
